params.question: What structural feature of amyloid fibrils makes them resistant to enzymatic degradation and insoluble in body fluids?

answers.text: Coating by serum amyloid P component that shields them from proteases

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: SAP binds all amyloid universally and is useful for scintigraphic imaging, but the resistance to proteolysis comes from the beta-sheet conformation of the fibrils themselves.
Correct. The cross-beta-pleated sheet arrangement makes amyloid fibrils insoluble and resistant to enzymatic breakdown, which is why deposits accumulate indefinitely once formed.

answers.text: Intracellular sequestration within lysosomes that shields them from extracellular proteases

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Amyloid is a pathological extracellular deposit. Its resistance to breakdown is intrinsic to the beta-sheet conformation, not due to intracellular location.

answers.text: Extensive branching of fibrils creating a dense protective meshwork

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Amyloid fibrils are non-branching and measure only 7.5–10 nm in diameter. Their stability comes from the cross-beta-pleated sheet structure, not from branching.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the structural basis of amyloid — all amyloid shares a cross-beta-pleated sheet conformation with non-branching fibrils (7.5–10 nm). This arrangement confers protease resistance and insolubility.
Well done! The cross-beta-pleated sheet conformation is the universal structural backbone of all amyloid, making it protease-resistant and insoluble regardless of the precursor protein.

params.question: A patient with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis develops nephrotic syndrome. A kidney biopsy shows apple-green birefringence with Congo red staining. Which precursor protein is most likely responsible?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Light chains cause AL amyloidosis, which arises from plasma cell dyscrasias such as multiple myeloma — not from chronic inflammatory conditions like rheumatoid arthritis.
Transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR) primarily affects the heart and peripheral nerves. It results from inherited mutations or age-related wild-type misfolding, not chronic inflammation.

Correct. Chronic inflammatory conditions like rheumatoid arthritis persistently elevate serum amyloid A, which misfolds into AA amyloid. The kidney is the organ most severely affected in AA amyloidosis.
Beta-2-microglobulin amyloidosis occurs in patients on long-term dialysis and typically causes joint disease — it is not associated with rheumatoid arthritis-driven chronic inflammation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the classification: AL arises from plasma cell dyscrasias (myeloma), AA from chronic inflammation (RA, TB, IBD), ATTR from transthyretin mutations or wild-type, and beta-2-microglobulin from long-term dialysis.
Well done! The clinical clue is chronic inflammation — rheumatoid arthritis drives persistent elevation of serum amyloid A, the precursor of AA amyloid, which preferentially deposits in the kidneys.

params.question: A patient with cardiac amyloidosis has an echocardiogram showing thickened ventricular walls, yet the ECG records low-voltage complexes. What explains this mismatch?

answers.text: Coexisting pericardial effusion is attenuating the ECG signals

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pericardial effusion can cause low ECG voltage, but it would not explain the thick ventricular walls seen on echocardiography. The mismatch requires an infiltrative explanation.

answers.text: Amyloid is electrically inert, so the thickened walls generate almost no electrical signal

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Amyloid deposits thicken the ventricular walls physically but are electrically inert — they do not generate electrical activity, producing the hallmark low-voltage ECG despite thick walls on echo.

answers.text: The cardiac conduction system has been destroyed by fibrous replacement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Conduction disease can occur in amyloidosis, but the specific voltage–wall thickness mismatch is best explained by the electrically inert nature of the amyloid infiltrate itself.

answers.text: Concentric myocardial hypertrophy produces paradoxically low ECG voltage

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: True myocardial hypertrophy produces high, not low, ECG voltage. The low-voltage pattern seen here points to an infiltrative process where the thickening material (amyloid) is electrically silent.

overallFeedback.feedback: In cardiac amyloidosis, the walls are thickened by amyloid infiltration, but since amyloid is electrically inert, it generates no electrical signal — hence low voltage on ECG despite thick walls on echocardiography.
Well done! This voltage–wall thickness mismatch is a clinical pearl — thick walls generating low voltage is a red flag for cardiac amyloidosis because amyloid is electrically inert.

interactions.label: Two patients both have Congo red-positive kidney biopsies showing apple-green bi

params.question: Two patients both have Congo red-positive kidney biopsies showing apple-green birefringence. One has AA amyloidosis from rheumatoid arthritis; the other has AL amyloidosis from myeloma. How does their treatment differ?

answers.text: Both receive the same immunosuppressive regimen since the Congo red deposits are histologically identical

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Congo red staining confirms the presence of amyloid but does not distinguish the type. Treatment must target the specific precursor protein and its underlying cause, which differs between AA and AL.

answers.text: AA is treated by controlling the underlying chronic inflammation; AL is treated by targeting the clonal plasma cells

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In AA amyloidosis, controlling the inflammatory stimulus reduces SAA production and halts further deposition. In AL amyloidosis, chemotherapy targets the plasma cell clone producing the pathogenic light chains.

answers.text: AA is treated with liver transplantation; AL is treated with long-term dialysis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Liver transplantation is used for hereditary transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis, where the liver produces the mutant protein. Long-term dialysis is associated with beta-2-microglobulin amyloidosis, not AL.

answers.text: AA responds to colchicine alone; AL requires no specific treatment beyond supportive care

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Colchicine is effective specifically in familial Mediterranean fever-associated AA amyloidosis but is not the universal AA treatment. AL amyloidosis requires aggressive anti-plasma-cell chemotherapy, not merely supportive care.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the treatment principle: Congo red unifies the diagnosis, but protein typing splits the treatment. AA amyloidosis requires controlling the underlying inflammation; AL amyloidosis requires targeting the plasma cell clone directly.
Well done! Congo red staining unifies the diagnosis, but treatment diverges: AA targets the source of chronic inflammation, while AL targets the clonal plasma cells producing pathogenic light chains.
